At the Foot of China Zun Stand at the foot of China Zun and look up at this towering skyscraper to feel its majesty and grandeur.
At night, China Zun is brightly lit, like a lighthouse illuminating the entire city.
You can use a wide-angle lens to capture the full view of China Zun, or choose a close-up lens to capture its unique architectural details.

📍 Top 5 Must-Visit Spots: Where Ancient Charm Meets Floral Splendor Temple of Heaven Apricot Blossom Forest Bloom Period: Late March to mid-April (best in late March) Features: Ancient Qing Dynasty apricot tree grove, nearly 200 century-old apricot trees intertwined with thousand-year-old cypresses, creating a dreamy pink and white floral sea.
Every shot is a classic ancient-style masterpiece!
Photo Spots: Apricot blossom forest east of the Science Park, Baihua Garden.
It is recommended to wear a light-colored long dress, with the ancient cypress forest as the background.
The morning light or twilight will make it even more dreamy.

Fenghuangling Apricot Blossom Valley Bloom Period: Late March to mid-April Scenery: The largest wild apricot forest in Beijing, with 600 acres of floral sea covering the valley, complemented by mountain streams, resembling a paradise.
Route: North Line hiking trail (Feilai Stone Pagoda for a panoramic view) + South Line original ecological floral sea.
It is recommended to drive or take a bus.
Badaling Great Wall Apricot Blossoms Bloom Period: Early to mid-April Features: Apricot blossoms and the Great Wall in the same frame, the cold stone walls set off the soft and beautiful floral sea.
It is recommended to take the S2 line "floral sea train" to take photos, and use sidelight to highlight the texture of the city walls.
Tips: Avoid peak crowds, and take photos in the early morning or after the rain for better shots.
Jinshanling Great Wall Apricot Blossoms Bloom Period: March 28 - April 11 (peak bloom April 4-8) Features: A rare and magnificent floral scene in the north.
The section from Zhuan Duokou to Shalingkou is a classic spot.
Xiaojinshan Tower overlooks the "Great Wall Dragon Traveling Through the Floral Sea." Note: Drones and camping are prohibited in the scenic area.
You need to make an appointment for the direct bus in advance.

Yuanmingyuan Apricot Blossom Spring Pavilion Bloom Period: Late March to early April Features: A garden named after apricot blossoms, with apricot blossoms by the pond reflecting the koi flower stream.
Drone aerial photography can capture the geometric aesthetics of the "Zen Floral Gallery." How to Play: Combine with the crabapples in Wenhua Hall to create a double floral sea experience.

The Summer Palace was first built in the 15th year of the Qianlong reign (1750) of the Qing Dynasty and was originally named the Qingyi Garden.
It was burned down by the Anglo-French Allied Forces in the 10th year of the Xianfeng reign (1860).

In the 12th year of the Guangxu reign (1886), the Qing court began to rebuild the Summer Palace with funds from the navy and other sources, and it was renamed two years later as a place for Empress Dowager Cixi to spend her later years.
In the 26th year of the Guangxu reign (1900), it was damaged again by the Eight-Nation Alliance, and was restored in the 28th year of the Guangxu reign (1902).

*   Taoranting Park | A hidden gem in Beijing!
🍂 Taoranting Park is a must-visit in Beijing during autumn!

As the autumn wind blows, the ginkgo trees turn yellow, creating a breathtaking autumn scene. 🎫 The ticket price is very affordable, only CNY 2, and annual cardholders can enter the park directly with their cards, making it a great value. 🚪 It is recommended to enter the park from the north gate, where you can immediately feel the strong autumn atmosphere.
The ginkgo avenue at the entrance is like a golden time tunnel, with golden ginkgo leaves swaying on the branches.

When the wind blows, the leaves fall like a golden rain, covering the ground with a thick "golden carpet." Walking on it, every step feels like stepping on the strings of autumn, playing a beautiful melody. 📸 Photo spots: - Ginkgo Avenue: Whether taking a portrait with the golden trees as the background or capturing the fallen leaves and pedestrians from above, you can capture the romance of autumn. - Xiehu Bridge: Standing on the bridge, you can enjoy the lake view and the colorful autumn trees on the shore, making it a great spot for taking backlit photos. - Canglang Pavilion: The ancient pavilion and red maple trees complement each other, with the fiery red leaves adding a touch of color to the ancient pavilion, making it a perfect spot for taking elegant autumn photos. 🍁 Travel route: Start your autumn journey from the north gate, walk slowly along the ginkgo avenue, immerse yourself in the golden world, and then head to Xiehu Bridge to enjoy the autumn scenery by the lake.
Then, stroll to Canglang Pavilion to experience the beauty of history and nature intertwined.
Afterward, you can visit the Rose Garden.
Although the roses in autumn are not as lush as during the peak blooming season, the remaining flowers and autumn branches have a unique charm.
Finally, head to the Huaxia Famous Pavilion Garden in the center of the park, where famous pavilions from all over the country are scattered among the colorful autumn trees.
You can rest in the pavilions and quietly enjoy the autumn scenery.
Visiting here with a few friends in autumn is a great choice!
